## Appearance

Diana Barry is a very pretty and vivacious girl noted for her expressive snap and color. She has black eyes, jet-black curls, and glossy tresses that frame her face. Her features are further characterized by bright rosy cheeks, a crimson complexion, and charming dimples.

## Personality

Diana is a cheerful, practical, and sweet-natured individual known for her humor and unselfish admiration of her friends' talents. She possesses a notable taste in dressing, making her advice on style frequently sought after. Additionally, she is deeply determined to ensure that her child's first memory of her is a pleasant one.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P9](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XXXVII. ## History

Diana Barry was named by a visiting schoolmaster when she was born. Growing up in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), she formed an intense childhood bond with [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), with whom she imagined ghosts in the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood), named local spots like Lover's Lane, and belonged to a [Story Club](../codex/factions.md#story-club). When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) moved to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), the two swore a vow of eternal friendship in the Barrys' garden. Despite a temporary separation enforced by her mother, Diana reunited with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) after [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) saved her baby sister [Minnie May](../character/minnie-may.md) from severe croup while their parents were away. Diana participated in local school activities, performing a solo at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) concert and later taking part in outings like discovering Hester Gray's garden.

As they grew older, Diana joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in co-founding and canvassing for the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvement-society). Together, they navigated rural adventures, such as attempting to buy a willow-ware platter from Miss [Sarah](../character/sarah.md) Copp in [Spencervale](../codex/places.md#spencervale) and taking an accidental detour to [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge) to meet Miss [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md). When [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) left for [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) while Diana stayed in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), the two maintained a close correspondence, keeping each other updated on community news, literary efforts, and personal developments. Diana eventually became secretly engaged to [Fred Wright](../character/fred-wright.md), a step that signaled shifting dynamics in their peer group. Shortly before Anne's second year at college, Diana and [Fred](../character/fred-wright.md) were married at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope) with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) assisting her as a bridesmaid. Following her wedding, Diana settled into her new home in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) and soon gave birth to a baby boy, whom [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) visited during her return home.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER II. Matthew Cuthbert Is Surprised P64](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0064), [v1 CHAPTER XII. ## Quotes

> "Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now."
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)

> “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue P24](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0024)

> “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically. “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.”
>
> — Diana Barry — [v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P49](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0049)

> "You’ll ruin your dress in that wet grain . . . ruin it. She doesn’t hear me! Well, she’ll never get that cow out by herself. I must go and help her, of course."
>
> — Diana Barry — [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P14](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0014)

> "I’ve heard mother speak of it but I never saw it before, and I wouldn’t have supposed that it could be in existence still. You’ve heard the story, Anne?"
>
> — Diana Barry — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P47](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0047)
